*Give Codex a task. Get verified changes and a draft pull request.*

> **Deliver only the current, checked and reviewed Git tree.**

## Why install this

Software Factory keeps a software task moving from investigation to an observed
draft PR in your current agent session. Its dependency-free Python engine keeps
the evidence ledger while Codex performs the reasoning, edits and native reviews.
It creates an isolated worktree, preserves your original checkout and makes
interrupted work resumable. Claude Code uses the same shared skill through a
compatibility adapter.

## What you get

| Capability | Result |
|---|---|
| Reviewed planning | Explicit acceptance criteria and repository instructions |
| Executable checks | Frozen commands, bounded logs and receipts for the current tree |
| Freshness checks | Edits require fresh verification and review before delivery |
| Recovery | Saved runs and idempotent delivery retries; failed attempts stay visible |
| Draft delivery | An observed branch, commit and open draft PR at the selected base |

```text
task → reviewed plan → implementation → executable checks → code review → draft PR
                              ↑                  │              │
                              └──────────────────┴──────────────┘
                                           repair
```

## Quick start

Install the root plugin once this layout is available on your selected Git revision:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add natejswenson/software-factory
codex plugin add software-factory@software-factory
codex plugin list --json
```

Start a fresh Codex session and ask: **“Use $software-factory in this repo to fix
[task]. Finish with verified changes and a draft PR.”** Review and commit the
project’s meaningful check configuration before starting. The skill selects the
engine from its loaded plugin root; a global `factory` is not required.

Invoke the skill in Codex:

```text
$software-factory Fix [task] in this repo and finish with a verified draft PR.
```

While this layout is under review, run from the reviewed repository checkout:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
codex plugin add software-factory@software-factory
```

See [installation from a reviewed checkout](docs/user-guide/installation.md#install-from-a-reviewed-checkout).
The [installation guide](docs/user-guide/installation.md) also covers native
updates, Claude compatibility, standalone uv/pip use and legacy manual skill links.

For Claude Code compatibility, install from the reviewed checkout:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add .
claude plugin install software-factory@software-factory
```

Restart Claude and invoke the plugin-qualified skill:

```text
/software-factory:software-factory Fix [task] in this repo and finish with a verified draft PR.
```

## Triggers

Use `$software-factory`, ask for a factory task, or ask the loaded skill to take
one request through verification and a draft PR. Saved runs can resume in a new
session. Three failed checks/reviews stop for explicit user direction; merging
and releasing are separate from the task’s draft endpoint.

## Requirements

Python 3.11+, Git and macOS/Linux. GitHub delivery also needs authenticated `gh`.
The engine needs no third-party runtime packages, Node, model API key or daemon.
Project checks may require their own dependencies. Existing runs retain their
original executable checks and evidence.

- **Codex:** Use native plugin commands, then start a fresh session with the loaded skill.
- **Claude Code:** Optional compatibility host; install the adapter and restart before invoking its skill.
- **Personal data:** Task state, logs and receipts stay under the repository’s Git common-dir in `factory/runs`, outside source. See [migration and updates](docs/user-guide/installation.md#update-and-activate).

## Changelog

Versioned changes and Python wheel/source archives are published in
[GitHub releases](https://github.com/natejswenson/software-factory/releases).

or in a released plugin revision.
